title: Choose the visual world for I-ITSM
question: The roll assigned The Scoreboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Scoreboard
options.lineage: hand-operated cricket ground scoreboards: painted green boards, hung white number plates
options.thesis: Every count, clock and incident number hangs as a white plate on a green board, readable from the far stand.
options.viewport: Green rail and a scoreboard strip of hung plates (open, breached, at risk, MTTR) over the triage queue; the single most urgent incident sits on the one reversed plate.
options.risk: Reads as a cricket gimmick if labels borrow cricket jargon; the world stays in type, colour and plates only.

raised.raise: One type family (Barlow and its condensed cuts) carries plates, headings, tables and captions; no second display face.
Plates change in a stepped two-frame flip; nothing in the app eases or fades.
Exactly one reversed plate per screen marks the single thing that needs attention now.
Hierarchy comes from scale contrast, huge plate numerals against small caps labels, not from boxes and cards.

options.label: Metro Line
options.lineage: city metro network maps and station signage
options.thesis: The incident lifecycle is a metro line: every incident is a train between named stations, Report to Close.
options.viewport: White ground, a top line diagram of the lifecycle with live counts at each station, the queue below with each row's position on the line.
options.risk: Familiar: service health as a transit map is where many ops dashboards land.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: Each screen hangs one yellow band naming the next decision; incident numbers set at gate-number scale.
options.viewport: A yellow decision band under the top bar ("3 incidents need you: INC1042 first, 12 min left"), queue rows led by monumental incident numbers.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity (one next decision per screen); loses on audience identification, airports are not the campus.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere turns to alarm fatigue unless it stays reserved for the next decision.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Incidents as registered plates on near-white stock.
options.viewport: A hairline grid of incident plates with a periwinkle stamp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an editorial annual neither speaks to campus IT nor reads as a working queue.
options.risk: Reads as a portfolio, not a tool.
options.kept: One type family carries display and caption alike.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as coloured tab boards under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail with the queue on a clear leaf.
options.case: Fuses poorly: layered leaves slow scanning; nobody here identifies with manuals.
options.risk: Ply logic adds visual depth to every table.
options.kept: Stepped two-frame changes with no easing.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides of incidents on a lit bed.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a single type size cannot carry a dashboard, and the rake fights tables.
options.kept: One reversed plate per screen for the most urgent item.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One incident fills the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A single incident filling the viewport with action glyphs on the right.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a queue needs comparison across rows, which one-at-a-time hides.
options.kept: The next incident is always one action away after resolving.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: A giant glyph with a breathing grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in IT incidents is a typeface.
options.risk: Pure type play with no product mechanism.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A service desk the way the leading ITSM products ship it, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, KPI cards row, filterable incident table with coloured status pills.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
